step1_analysis.description: A single PMOS transistor configured as a source follower. Given the context of a downconverter, this is likely an extracted output buffer or a test structure used to drive off-chip loads.

paper_reference.title: A 410-mW 1.22-GHz Downconverter in a Dual-Conversion Tuner IC for OpenCable Applications

voltage_gain.description: Low-frequency voltage gain of the source follower

sky130_expected.calculation: Assuming 100uA bias and VIN_DC=0.5V: gm = 2*Id/Vov ≈ 317uS. Gain = gm*ro/(1+gm*ro) ≈ 0.97 V/V = -0.26 dB
sky130_expected.reasoning: A source follower inherently has a voltage gain slightly less than unity (0 dB) due to body effect and finite output resistance.

sky130_expected.calculation: BW = gm / (2*pi*Cload). With Cload = 1pF and gm = 317uS, BW ≈ 50 MHz
sky130_expected.reasoning: Bandwidth is heavily dependent on the load capacitance. A 1pF load yields ~50MHz, which is sufficient for the 44 MHz IF mentioned in the paper.

dc_power.description: DC power consumption of the buffer stage

sky130_expected.reasoning: Determined by the bias current provided in the testbench to keep the PMOS in saturation.

step3_testbench.description: Testbench for the PMOS Source Follower measuring AC gain, bandwidth, transient swing, and DC power.
step3_testbench.spice:
* PMOS Source Follower Testbench
.param W_xm1=5u L_xm1=0.5u

* DUT
XM1 N0 N1 VOUT VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm1} w={W_xm1}

* Sources and Biasing
VN0 N0 0 0
VVDD VDD 0 1.8
* DC bias of 0.5V ensures PMOS stays in saturation (VOUT will be ~1.5V)
VVIN N1 0 DC 0.5 AC 1 SIN(0.5 0.1 1MEG 0 0)
IBIAS VDD VOUT 100u
CLOAD VOUT 0 1p

.lib "${SKY130_PDK}" tt

.control
* 1. DC Operating Point & Power
op
let power = -i(VVDD)*1.8
print power

* 2. AC Analysis for Gain and Bandwidth
ac dec 10 1k 1G
let gain_db = vdb(VOUT)
meas ac mid_gain find gain_db at=10k
* Assuming mid_gain is approx -0.5dB, -3dB point is at -3.5dB
meas ac bw when gain_db=-3.5 fall=1

* 3. Transient Analysis for Output Swing
tran 1n 5u
meas tran vout_max max v(VOUT)
meas tran vout_min min v(VOUT)
let swing = vout_max - vout_min
print swing

quit
.endc
